text: The paper defines (ε,δ)-recovery complexity to measure the time an algorithm needs to reach target accuracy after a distribution shift, and (ε,ρ)-TTA learnability to quantify long-term reliability across a full non-stationary stream (Section 2).

Theorem 3.3 establishes a minimax lower bound showing recovery complexity scales as 1/α² with alignment strength α, inversely with batch size B, and directly with a temporal correlation factor C_φ derived from φ-mixing conditions (Theorem 3.3).
Theorem 3.9 shows a simple gradient-based test-time adaptation baseline achieves an upper bound of O((C_φ/B)·log((Δ_W+ε)/ε)/(α²ε)), matching the lower bound up to logarithmic factors (Theorem 3.9).

Theorem 4.3 (Transfer Theorem) converts local recovery guarantees into global (ε,ρ)-learnability results by relating shift count and per-shift recovery time to the overall violation rate (Theorem 4.3).

Synthetic experiments confirm the predicted scaling laws τ ∝ 1/α² and τ ∝ 1/B, and real-world evaluations on CIFAR-10-C and ImageNet-C show the Tent method exhibits positive proxy-task alignment under moderate shift but negative alignment (and collapse) under strong temporal correlation (Section 5).
